what_it_does: Operating systems — the software layer (like Linux or Windows) that manages everything running on a computer — have millions of lines of code and have been a perpetual target for hackers. Formally proving that a piece of software is correct means using mathematical logic to guarantee, not just test, that it behaves securely. This paper surveys the seL4 project, which produced such proofs for a small but real operating system kernel called seL4. The proof chain goes all the way from the human-readable C source code down to the binary instructions the processor actually executes, across four different processor architectures, and includes guarantees about confidentiality and integrity. The paper then discusses very early-stage thinking about whether this methodology could eventually scale to a full general-purpose OS.
